sections.h2: What makes Riviera Beach a distinct setting for a home sale in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
Riviera Beach is a compact waterfront city in Palm Beach County, on 8.28 square miles, with an estimated 39,357 residents in July 2025, according to the Census Bureau. The city's economic page calls it the Best Waterfront City in which to live, work and play and puts its year-round average temperature at 75 degrees.

The Port of Palm Beach sits inside the city limits, and the city says a cruise ship sails from there every other day. The city's police history says Riviera Beach took in the larger part of south central Singer Island in the early 1940s, so the city spans both the barrier island and the mainland. Sellers here commonly consider three routes.

  • Hiring an agent and waiting on a conventional buyer.
  • Selling directly to a buyer you find yourself.
  • Accepting a cash purchase that takes the house as it stands, on a schedule you control.

sections.h2: How did Riviera Beach grow from a fishing and resort town?
sections.html:
A county history page says Judge Allen Heyser renamed the Oak Lawn Hotel and post office Riviera in 1893, and Charles N. Newcomb bought the hotel in 1901 and recorded a plat in 1913 aiming at a resort community. Fishing families, many from the Bahamas, lived at the south end of Singer Island by 1906, and the page says Riviera Beach later became one of the largest fish suppliers on Florida's east coast.

The city's police history says 26 qualified voters met on September 29, 1922 to incorporate the town. In the early 1940s it took in the larger part of south central Singer Island and became Riviera Beach, and in 1959 it became a city. Its population passed 4,000 during World War II and the city police were covering over 13,000 residents in that era.

The city's economic development page also points readers to a 1976 booklet, A History of Riviera Beach, Florida, from the Bicentennial Commission, which it posts as a PDF for anyone curious about the neighborhoods behind an address. That layered history leaves a mix of lot sizes, ages and styles, so condition and exact location drive price more than a citywide figure.

sections.h2: How do Palm Beach County homestead rules apply when a Riviera Beach owner sells?
sections.html:
Palm Beach's property appraiser says a homestead applies a $25,000 exemption to the first $50,000 of assessed value for all taxes, plus an additional exemption that is not applied to school taxes and has a 2025 maximum of $25,722. Applications must be eligible as of January 1 and submitted by March 1.

The office renews qualifying exemptions automatically and mails a receipt card on the last business day of December. If ownership changes by sale, marriage, divorce or death, or the use changes, the owner should call the office or email it. The page also notes that a homestead does not move to a new residence, so a buyer files separately.

Save Our Homes holds yearly assessed-value growth to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and the Department of Revenue says a sale resets the property to just value. Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, according to a Volusia appraiser's summary, so ask Palm Beach's office how its larger exemption will apply from 2027.

Filing choices include the online E File system, five service centers or a mailed form, and the office lists 561.355.2866 for ownership changes. Applicants need Social Security numbers for all owners and spouses, a Florida driver's license and one more proof of residence such as a voter registration or a utility bill for the property.

  • Report a move-out so the exemption ends cleanly.
  • Ask about portability if you are buying another Florida homestead.

sections.h2: What if property taxes on a Riviera Beach house go unpaid?
sections.html:
Taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and the county tax collector sells tax certificates on unpaid items by June 1. The certificate goes to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, bid in quarter-percent steps (section 197.432).

A certificate holder may file for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the year of issuance, with a $75 application fee under section 197.502. For a homestead, the opening bid adds one-half of the latest assessed value to the amounts due. The clerk then holds a public auction, and the high bidder posts the larger of 5 percent or $200 and pays the rest within 24 hours, excluding weekends and holidays.

If you carry a certificate on your house, a sale before the deed process can protect what equity remains. Ask the Palm Beach tax collector for the redemption total, since that amount is not something to estimate.

sections.h2: What deed, recording and landlord points matter in Riviera Beach?
sections.html:
With a renter share near two in five, many Riviera Beach houses are sold with tenants. For a month-to-month tenancy, Florida requires at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period, and after a court judgment the sheriff acts on the writ after 24 hours' posted notice (sections 83.57 and 83.62).

Outside Miami-Dade a deed bears 70 cents of stamp tax for each $100, paid to the clerk at recording, and every signer is liable. Section 28.24 sets recording at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, plus technology charges.

  • Request lien payoffs and a tax proration from the closing agent.
  • Collect leases and deposit records for the buyer.
  • Locate the two witnesses needed for the deed.

sections.h2: Does living near the port or Singer Island affect how a house is marketed?
sections.html:
It does. The city's own economic page frames the port as part of the waterfront identity, and the city says the waterfront marketplace draws visitors headed for the cruise ships. Properties near the water or the marinas get compared on views, boat access and insurance costs, while inland properties are compared on lot size, roof age and distance to the bridges.

Gather your flood zone information, insurance policy and permit records before talking price, so a buyer can judge ongoing costs along with the sale price.

faqs.q: Is a tenant-occupied Riviera Beach house sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease generally runs on until its term or a proper notice ends it, so hand the buyer's title agent the lease, deposit records and any management agreement.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my Palm Beach homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The property appraiser's page says homestead does not transfer to a new residence, and a sale or other ownership change should be reported to the office.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax rate on a Riviera Beach deed?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue lists 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, and all parties to the document are liable.

faqs.q: When do unpaid property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1, per the Department of Revenue. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale quicker than listing here?
faqs.a: Often, because no lender appraisal is needed. Title still has to be clear and the deed witnessed and recorded before closing.
